title: The Joyal model structure and its fibrant objects
statement:
Use simplicial sets, standard simplices, inner horns, quasicategories and universes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For a simplicial set $S$, let $hS$ be the category generated by its vertices and edges, with degenerate edges identified with identities and each $2$-simplex imposing the relation that its long edge is the composite of its other two edges. Write $\operatorname{Fun}(A,C)_n=\operatorname{Hom}(A\times\Delta^n,C)$. A simplicial map $u:A\to B$ is a categorical equivalence if restriction induces an equivalence of ordinary categories $h\operatorname{Fun}(B,C)\to h\operatorname{Fun}(A,C)$ for every quasicategory $C$ (in any sufficiently large universe).

In each universe the category of simplicial sets admits the Joyal model structure: cofibrations are degreewise injective maps, weak equivalences are these categorical equivalences, and fibrations have the right lifting property against the cofibrations that are categorical equivalences. Here a lifting problem is a commutative square, and a lift is a diagonal making its two triangles commute. The classes of weak equivalences have two-out-of-three and are retract closed. Every arrow factors functorially both as a cofibration followed by a trivial fibration and as a trivial cofibration followed by a fibration; trivial means also a weak equivalence. The pairs (cofibrations, trivial fibrations) and (trivial cofibrations, fibrations) are weak factorization systems: either class is exactly the class having the appropriate left or right lifting property against the other. These factorizations take place in the given universe. Every inner horn inclusion is a trivial cofibration. A simplicial set is fibrant, meaning its map to the terminal simplicial set is a fibration, if and only if it is a quasicategory.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.5.1, Lemma 2.2.5.2, Proposition 2.2.5.8 and Theorem 2.4.6.1; online PDF pp. 106-112 and 153-154 (printed pp. 89-95,136-137). No Stacks tag states the Joyal model structure.

proof.text: For any quasicategory $C$ and simplicial set $K$, $C^K=\operatorname{Fun}(K,C)$ is a quasicategory. An inner-horn lifting problem in $C^K$ transposes to extension into $C$ across the pushout product of that horn with $\varnothing\to K$. An inner horn is inner anodyne by the lifting definitions in [lem-coef-inner-anodyne-pushout-product]; that node makes the pushout product inner anodyne. The map $C\to *$ is an inner fibration by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], hence gives the extension. Currying and permutation of product factors give natural simplicial isomorphisms $(C^B)^K\cong(C^K)^B$, commuting with restriction in $B$.

source.place: Corollaries 3.2.4 and 3.2.10; the model-independent proof of HTT Proposition 1.2.7.3(1), not its model-dependent clauses (2)-(3).

proof.text: Use the invertible interval $J$ and endpoints of [lem-coef-quasicategory-invertible-interval], and put $\delta:\{0,1\}\hookrightarrow J$. For a map $i:U\hookrightarrow V$, put $i\in\mathcal T$ when $C^V\to C^U$ is a trivial Kan fibration for every quasicategory $C$ in the fixed universe. The interval lemma states that $C^J\to C$ is a trivial Kan fibration for each endpoint. Hence $e_\varepsilon\square j\in\mathcal T$ for every monomorphism $j$: the boundary lifting problem transposes to lifting $j\square(\partial\Delta^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m)$ against $C^J\to C$. This pushout product is a monomorphism degreewise, since its source is a union of subsets of the product target. The lift is supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-lifts-monomorphisms]. Also every inner horn $i$ belongs to $\mathcal T$: its boundary lifting problems transpose to $i\square(\partial\Delta^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m)$ into $C$, and [lem-coef-inner-anodyne-pushout-product] makes this inner anodyne. Here $m=0$ is included and gives vertex surjectivity, exactly as required by [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration].

source.place: Corollary 3.5.13 for the endpoint; Corollary 3.2.4 for horns; direct transposed boundary lifting.

proof.text: The class $\mathcal T$ is weakly saturated and satisfies $i\square j\in\mathcal T$ whenever $i\in\mathcal T$ and $j$ is a monomorphism. For saturation, boundary lifting of $C^V\to C^U$ says precisely that $i$ has the left lifting property against each $C^{\Delta^m}\to C^{\partial\Delta^m}$. A fixed left lifting class is closed under pushout by restricting a square, under transfinite composition by extending the diagonal at successor stages and taking its compatible union at limits, and under retract by composing with section and retraction; isomorphisms lift by inverses. Monomorphisms are closed under these operations degreewise. For the pushout product assertion, a boundary lifting problem for $C^{\operatorname{cod}(i\square j)}\to C^{\operatorname{dom}(i\square j)}$ transposes, by associativity and symmetry of product, to lifting $j\square(\partial\Delta^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m)$ against $C^V\to C^U$. That map is a monomorphism, and [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-lifts-monomorphisms] gives the lift. This uses boundary dimension zero as well as the positive dimensions.

source.place: Elementary lifting-class and pushout-product adjunction arguments; compare Definition 2.4.11.

proof.text: Let $M=\{\partial\Delta^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m:m\geq0\}$. Define a small set $\Lambda_0$ consisting of all inner horns and the maps $e_\varepsilon\square b$ for $b\in M$, $\varepsilon=0,1$; define $\Lambda_{r+1}=\{\delta\square a:a\in\Lambda_r\}$, and let $\mathrm{An}$ be the weakly saturated closure of $\bigcup_{r\geq0}\Lambda_r$. All generators belong to $\mathcal T$ by steps 2-3, so $\mathrm{An}\subseteq\mathcal T$. This is a small generating set of monomorphisms in the input universe, since it is a countable union of small sets and uses only small products and pushouts. We verify the two interval axioms of [lem-coef-presheaf-cylinder-model-recognition]. By [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells], every monomorphism is built from boundary inclusions by coproducts, pushouts and countable composition. For a fixed map $v$, the operation $v\square(-)$ preserves these colimit attachments and retracts: degreewise product with a fixed set preserves colimits, and the pushout formula gives the corresponding pushout for each attachment. More explicitly, along an increasing chain $K_\alpha$ with final union $L$, filter the source-to-target map for $v:U\to V$ by $(V\times K_\alpha)\cup(U\times L)$; the successor attachment is a pushout of $v\square(K_\alpha\to K_{\alpha+1})$, and limits are unions. A cobase change of a map gives a cobase change of its pushout product by the same union formula. Thus $e_\varepsilon\square j\in\mathrm{An}$ for every monomorphism $j$. For the second axiom, each generator $a\in\Lambda_r$ satisfies $\delta\square a\in\Lambda_{r+1}\subseteq\mathrm{An}$. The displayed filtration with $v=\delta$ expresses the pushout product of a composite of cell attachments as successive pushouts of the pushout products of those attachments, with unions at limit stages. Cobase changes are carried to cobase changes by the union formula above. Functoriality carries a section-retraction pair of arrows to a section-retraction pair, so retracts are preserved as well. Closure of $\mathrm{An}$ under these operations therefore gives $\delta\square a\in\mathrm{An}$ for every $a\in\mathrm{An}$. Coproducts can be expressed as composites of the individual pushouts after well-ordering the small indexing set.

source.place: Example 2.4.13, with the generating set taken to be all inner horns; the recursive generators and both closure axioms are checked explicitly.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-presheaf-cylinder-model-recognition] to presheaves on the simplex category, the interval $J$ and the class $\mathrm{An}$ of step 4. The endpoint union $\Delta^0\amalg\Delta^0\to J$ is a monomorphism, because its degreewise images are the distinct constant simplices at 0 and 1. The needed interval axioms were verified in step 4. The naive fibrant objects are precisely the quasicategories. Indeed $\mathrm{An}$ contains all inner horns, so a naive fibrant object fills them. Conversely, for a quasicategory $C$ and $a:U\hookrightarrow V$ in $\mathrm{An}\subseteq\mathcal T$, the map $C^V\to C^U$ is surjective on vertices by [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration]; hence every map $U\to C$ extends strictly over $V$. This is exactly the required terminal-map lifting property. We have therefore constructed a model structure with monomorphism cofibrations, fibrant objects the quasicategories, and weak equivalences $W_J$ detected by bijectivity of $[B,C]_J\to[A,C]_J$ for every quasicategory $C$. The bracket denotes maps modulo finite chains of $J$-homotopies, as defined in the recognition node. Every inner horn is a trivial cofibration, since it belongs to $\mathrm{An}$.

source.place: Theorem 2.4.19 and Proposition 2.4.25; the specialization and fibrant identification are proved here, before comparing weak equivalence conventions.

proof.text: We now identify $W_J$ with the testing class $W$ in the statement. By step 1, $C^K$ is a quasicategory. By [lem-coef-quasicategory-invertible-interval], its vertices are isomorphic in $h(C^K)$ exactly when joined by a $J$-map; after currying, this says that $[K,C]_J$ is exactly the set of isomorphism classes of objects of $h(C^K)$. Consequently $u\in W$ implies $u\in W_J$. Conversely let $u:A\to B$ belong to $W_J$, fix a quasicategory $C$, and put $D=C^B$, $E=C^A$, $p=u^*:D\to E$. For every simplicial set $K$, currying identifies $[K,D]_J\to[K,E]_J$ with $[B,C^K]_J\to[A,C^K]_J$, which is bijective since $C^K$ is another test. Taking $K=E$ gives a map $s:E\to D$ with $ps\sim_J1_E$. Taking $K=D$ and using injectivity shows $sp\sim_J1_D$, because $p(sp)=(ps)p\sim_Jp=p1_D$. These relations are finite chains of actual $J$-homotopies. Every $H:T\times J\to T'$ induces a natural isomorphism on the categories generated by vertices, edges and triangles: the two inverse edges of $J$ and their inverse triangles give inverse components at each vertex of $T$, and the two triangular faces subdividing an edge of $T$ times $\Delta^1$ give naturality for each edge generator. The naturality equation respects the defining triangle relations. Applying this to the chains gives $h(ps)\cong1_{hE}$ and $h(sp)\cong1_{hD}$. Thus $hp$ is an ordinary equivalence with quasi-inverse $hs$, which proves $u\in W$. This comparison uses no rigidification theorem or previously named Joyal model structure.

source.place: Direct Yoneda calculation in the category modulo interval homotopy; compare Theorem 3.6.8. No use of its model-dependent proof or of HTT Proposition 2.2.5.8.

proof.text: The model structure constructed in step 5, together with $W_J=W$ from step 6, has exactly the cofibrations, weak equivalences and fibrations required by the statement. The two weak factorization systems and their functorial factorizations, as well as two-out-of-three and retract closure, are the explicit conclusions of [lem-coef-presheaf-cylinder-model-recognition]. The factorizations stay in the input universe. Its fibrant-object assertion combined with the terminal lifting calculation in step 5 gives the required if and only if for quasicategories, and the last sentence of step 5 gives every inner horn as a trivial cofibration. Completeness and cocompleteness are also literal: degreewise set limits and colimits carry induced simplicial operators, and the universal properties are verified degreewise.

source.place: Assembly of Theorem 2.4.19 after the testing-class comparison; no model axiom is assumed in the comparison.

proof.text: Finally, the testing condition is invariant under enlargement of universe. A map from a small simplicial set into a larger quasicategory $C$ factors through a small subquasicategory: start with its simplicial image, repeatedly adjoin one filler in $C$ for every inner horn in the current subset, and take the union over the natural numbers. Finite horns ensure that every horn in the union already occurs at one stage; smallness is preserved at each stage and at the union. Relabel its degree sets by small bijective copies if their elements are outside the smaller universe. For a small $u:A\to B$ satisfying the small-universe tests, fix a larger test $C$. Essential surjectivity of $h(C^B)\to h(C^A)$ follows by factoring the data of a map $A\to C$ through such a small quasicategory $C_0$ and using its small-universe testing equivalence. For fullness, fix two maps $B\to C$ and a morphism between their restrictions in $h(C^A)$. That morphism is a finite path of edge generators, hence is represented by finitely many maps $A\times\Delta^1\to C$. Factor both maps on $B$ and these finitely many maps through one small $C_0$, and use fullness of $h(C_0^B)\to h(C_0^A)$. For faithfulness, fix two morphisms in $h(C^B)$ whose restrictions are equal. Each is a finite path of maps $B\times\Delta^1\to C$; their equality after restriction is witnessed by finitely many applications of identity and triangle relations, involving finitely many maps $A\times\Delta^2\to C$. Put all this data in one small $C_0$. The equality then holds in $h(C_0^A)$, so faithfulness there proves equality in $h(C_0^B)$ and hence in $h(C^B)$. Thus all three ordinary equivalence conditions hold for larger $C$. Restricting tests gives the converse. The class constructed in the fixed universe is therefore the larger-universe class in the statement.

source.place: Agent-written small-subquasicategory and finite generators-and-relations argument; uses only finite horns and the definition of h, not factorizations or HTT comparison theorems.
